chunks: Inductor impedance from DC to ∞. The question: What is an inductors impedance at DC vs infinitely high frequency? Plot this behavior.
Impedance is how strongly a part opposes alternating current at a given frequency. For an inductor, that opposition grows as the frequency goes up.
At DC the inductor opposes nothing and acts like a wire. At very high frequency it opposes almost everything and acts like a gap.
This page asks you to describe and sketch that rise.
Think of pushing a heavy swing. Push slowly and it follows along easily, so it feels no resistance.
Push back and forth faster and faster, and the heavy swing fights every reversal harder and harder.
The coil works the same way: more current reversals per second means more pushback.
The analogy only covers the ideal coil: a real one has small extra effects that matter at both ends of the frequency range.
A straight line through the origin with slope 2πL about 62. 8 ohms per MHz. Zero at DC, growing without limit as frequency rises.
Impedance ( Z ): the opposition to AC current, in ohms. It is the AC version of resistance. Reactance: the part of impedance that comes from storing energy.
For an inductor it is omega L . Frequency ( f ): how many cycles per second the signal makes. Here omega equals 2 pi f . Inductor impedance: Z L equals j omega L .
Its size is omega L ; the j just marks that the voltage peaks a quarter cycle ahead of the current.
Self-resonant frequency: the frequency where the tiny capacitance between a real coil's turns takes over from the inductance.
Take a 1 millihenries inductor. At 0 hertz its impedance is 0 ohms, a short. At 1 kilohertz, omega L equals 2 pi times 1000 times 0. 001 about 6. 3 ohms.
At 10 kilohertz it is ten times more, about 63 ohms. At 100 kilohertz it is about 630 ohms.
Each ten-fold step in frequency gives a ten-fold step in impedance, which is a straight line going up on a log-log plot. That is the whole idea.
"At DC an ideal inductor's impedance j omega L is zero, a short; as frequency goes to infinity it goes to infinity, an open.
Plotted, Z is a straight line through the origin, or on log–log axes a line rising at 20 decibels per decade with a constant +90° phase.
A real inductor bottoms out at its DCR at low frequency, peaks at its self-resonant frequency because of winding capacitance, and turns capacitive above it."
